title: Know Who You Are Dealing With – Do Not Offend the Wrong Person
summary: It is crucial to know the type of person you are dealing with before attempting any deception or application of law. The text categorizes five distinct types of people: the arrogant and proud man (sensitive to insults and quick to seek vengeance), the insecure man (relentlessly revengeful once harmed), Mr. Suspicious (paranoid and easily manipulated), the serpent with a long memory (patiently waits for the right time to strike back after an insult), and the plain, natural man (unaware and unpredictable, making him a waste of time and energy to deceive). Success requires gathering facts, using spies, and never relying solely on intuition or appearances.
example: Genghis Khan conquered and destroyed the Shah Empire after Muhammad killed his messenger and insulted him.
A man scammed of $45,000 relentlessly tracked down and jailed a ring of American con artists.
The King of Cheng insulted an exiled prince of Chin, who later gained power and destroyed Cheng in revenge.
Five art dealers failed to deceive Henry Ford because his simple, pragmatic nature rendered their elaborate sales pitch a complete waste of effort.
reversal: This law has no reversal because nothing good can come from failing to identify the person you are dealing with.
